items.stem: A levelling loop that starts and ends on the same benchmark does not close back to the same value. What does this misclosure indicate?

options.text: Accumulated measurement error that must be checked and, if within tolerance, distributed
options.rationale: Correct: misclosure reveals error to be checked and adjusted within tolerance.

options.text: That the benchmark physically moved during the hour
options.rationale: A moved benchmark is rare; the usual cause is measurement error.

options.text: That levelling is impossible on that site
options.rationale: Misclosure is normal and managed, not a sign levelling is impossible.

options.text: That the Earth is not round
options.rationale: Earth curvature is negligible at this scale and not the cause.

items.explanation: Correct: misclosure reveals error to be checked and adjusted within tolerance.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when setting out a building? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Work from established control points, not from other new work
options.rationale: Correct: setting out from control limits error propagation.

options.text: Independently check each set-out dimension or angle
options.rationale: Correct: independent checks catch blunders before they are built.

options.text: Measure once and never verify to save time
options.rationale: Single unverified measurements risk undetected blunders.

options.text: Use a different datum for each trade
options.rationale: Multiple datums introduce avoidable positional errors.

items.explanation: Correct: setting out from control limits error propagation.

items.stem: What is the purpose of a benchmark on a construction site?

options.text: To provide a known reference level from which other levels are measured
options.rationale: Correct: a benchmark is a fixed reference for levels.

options.text: To mark where the site canteen will go
options.rationale: A benchmark is a survey reference, not a facility marker.

options.text: To record the contractor's best achievement
options.rationale: That is an unrelated colloquial meaning.
A benchmark is a reference point, not storage.

items.explanation: Correct: a benchmark is a fixed reference for levels.
